title: Illustration: Masterbrand Color Alternate Stripes
slide_intent: Simplify a graphic when its setting demands clarity so people can recognize the brand on uniforms and directional surfaces.
strategic_value: Four ordered brand colors can preserve Burger King recognition where the more detailed ingredient stripes would be cumbersome.
demonstration: A four-band horizontal specimen sits above restaurant frontage, ground-direction and uniform examples; the left text defines when the alternate stripes apply.
practical_value: Choose the alternate four-color treatment for applications requiring simplicity and preserve its stated color order.

content_islands.name: Alternate-stripe guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the scope and ordered color list in the left column.

content_islands.name: Four-color specimen
content_islands.spec: Show cream, orange, red and brown horizontal bands across the upper right.

content_islands.name: Application examples
content_islands.spec: Group a restaurant and directional-ground treatment with uniform photographs below the specimen.

reference_purposes.Intent: The copy explains that alternate stripes serve instances where simplicity is required, such as uniforms and directional stripes.
reference_purposes.Expression: The specimen reduces the motif to four straight color bands.
reference_purposes.Application: Restaurant, directional and uniform examples show the alternate treatment in context.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The specified order is Mayo Egg White, Flaming Orange, Fiery Red and BBQ Brown.

ingredient.name: Alternate masterbrand stripes
ingredient.role: Provide a simpler identifying color sequence.
ingredient.application: Use four colors in order: Mayo Egg White, Flaming Orange, Fiery Red, BBQ Brown.
ingredient.scope: For instances requiring simplicity, including uniforms and directional stripes; this does not replace primary illustration stripes everywhere.
